newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs end flat ahead last day of trade in 1996.
newsitem.headline: OLOs end flat ahead last day of trade in 1996.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds are expected to move sideways on Tuesday, the last day of trade in 1996 when the market will close early.
The market will be closed all day on Wednesday for New Year's Day.
But dealers expected the start to the New Year on Thursday to be lively, with some profit taking hitting prices before the uptrend is re-established.
The benchmark 10-year bond yield ended a thin session Monday at 5.87 percent, down from 5.88 on Friday, with the spread over similar Bunds an unchanged nine basis points.
Dealers mostly expect yields to rise slightly at the start of 1997 as investors, who have not taken capital gains in 1996 because of potential tax liabilities, unwind some positions.
But with money market rates expected to stay firmly around 3.00 percent for the first half of the year, most expect any cash from profit-taking to be quickly reinvested in the OLO market.
"Maybe in the first week there might be some profit-taking but after that I think yields will continue to go down," one trader said.
